core.listContexts: List the spaces (clients, projects, areas of life) of one side: private (personal life) or pro (work). Use it to get the exact space names before filtering or filing tasks by space. Returns each space with its id, name, side and position.
core.setLocale: Switch the app interface language to French or English. Use it only when the user asks to change the language of the app. Returns the language now applied.

tasks.list: List active tasks, subtasks included unless topLevelOnly is true, filtered by side, space name, status categories, tag, latest due date or text in the title. Completed and canceled tasks are excluded unless requested. Use it to find tasks and their ids, or with side, query and topLevelOnly to pick a parent task. Returns the tasks sorted by due date then priority, and truncated: true when more tasks match than the limit.
tasks.get: Get one active task by its id, with its notes, tags, active subtasks, relations (blocks, blockedBy and related: the other tasks, active and on the same side) and blocked (true when the task is open and an open task blocks it). Use it to see the current state of a task before changing it. Returns the task, or the error not_found when it does not exist or is in the trash.
tasks.listDueToday: List the open tasks that are overdue or due today in the user time zone, on both sides, subtasks included. Use it to answer what needs to be done today. Returns the tasks sorted by due date, due time and priority.
tasks.listTrash: List the tasks in the trash, subtasks included, most recently trashed first. Use it to find a task to restore. Returns each task with the time it was moved to the trash.
tasks.listTags: List all tag names of the workspace. Use it to reuse an existing tag instead of creating a near duplicate. Returns each tag with its id and name.
tasks.create: Create a task, or a subtask of a top-level task with parentId. Use it when the user wants to note something to do. A top-level task needs a side or a space name; a subtask takes the side and space of its parent, and its priority unless a priority is given (0 included); tags are not inherited and later priority changes are not propagated. Unknown tag names are created. Returns the created task with its tags.
tasks.update: Change the title, notes, side, space, status category, priority, due date or due time of an active task. Use it to edit an existing task; add or remove tags by name with addTags and removeTags, other tags are kept. The side and space of a subtask follow its parent and cannot be changed. Returns the updated task.
tasks.complete: Mark an active task as completed. Use it when the user says a task is done. Its subtasks keep their status. Returns the updated task.
tasks.moveToTrash: Move an active task to the trash, together with its active subtasks. Use it when the user wants to remove a task; nothing is deleted and tasks.restore brings it back. Returns the task id and the number of subtasks moved with it.
tasks.restore: Restore a task from the trash, with the subtasks moved to the trash at the same time. Use it to bring back a task removed by mistake. A subtask whose parent is in the trash cannot be restored alone. Returns the restored task.
tasks.move: Move an active task or subtask on the board: set its status category (the column) and its place in that column. Use it to change a status by moving a card or to reorder a column: beforeId and afterId are the neighbouring cards (just above and just below the new place), omit both for the top of the column, and the position is ignored in completed and canceled. Returns the updated task, or the error not_found when it does not exist or is in the trash; a neighbour that is no longer in the column is ignored.
tasks.setParent: Attach an active task to a parent task, move it to another parent, or detach it with parentId null so that it becomes a top-level task again. Use it to turn a task into a subtask or back: only one level is allowed, the parent must be an active top-level task on the same side (private or pro), and the task keeps its status, position, priority, tags and relations. The task takes the space of the parent and loses its space when the parent has none; detaching does not give it back. Returns the updated task, or the error not_found when the task or the parent does not exist or when the task is in the trash; refused when parentId equals taskId (invalid_params), when the task has active subtasks (has_subtasks: detach them first), when it has no active subtask but subtasks in the trash (has_trashed_subtasks: the trash cannot be emptied, so restore each one with tasks.restore, then detach it with parentId null; tasks.listTrash lists them), or when the parent is itself a subtask (subtask_depth), on the other side (cross_side_parent) or in the trash (parent_in_trash).
tasks.addRelation: Link two active tasks on the same side (private or pro), subtasks included. Use it to record that a task blocks another or that two tasks are related: kind is read from taskId to otherTaskId, so blocks means taskId blocks otherTaskId, blocked_by means taskId is blocked by otherTaskId, and related is symmetric. Returns the task taskId with its relations, unchanged and without error when the relation already exists, or the error not_found when one of the two tasks does not exist or is in the trash; refused when otherTaskId equals taskId (invalid_params), when the two tasks are on different sides (cross_side_relation) or when the opposite blocking relation already exists (relation_conflict).
tasks.removeRelation: Remove a relation between two active tasks, described like in tasks.addRelation (blocked_by from A to B removes B blocks A). Use it when a task no longer blocks another or is no longer related to it. Returns the task taskId with its remaining relations, or the error not_found when the relation does not exist or when one of the two tasks is in the trash: restore that task with tasks.restore first, then remove the relation.
tasks.listBoard: Get the board of one side (private or pro): one column per status category, in board order (backlog, unstarted, started, completed, canceled). Use it to see tasks by status or to find the neighbouring cards before tasks.move; a subtask is a card of its own unless includeSubtasks is false, and hideCompletedSubtasks leaves completed subtasks out. Returns each column with its tasks in display order, its total and truncated: true when it holds more tasks than returned; open columns return up to 200 cards in manual order, completed and canceled the 20 most recently closed unless completedLimit or canceledLimit says otherwise.
